metadata.ageAEventSeeding: Shuffle the Age A military deck (10 event cards); place the top (players+2) cards face down as the current events deck (2p:4, 3p:5, 4p:6). Return the rest to the box unseen. No one ever draws Age A military cards.
metadata.tacticsRules2015: Playing a tactic from hand costs 1 military action (Action Phase). After you replenish the card row at the start of your next turn (before your Politics Phase) the card moves to the common tactics area, where any player may copy it for 2 military actions. Age II/III tactics show a second, lesser strength used for outdated armies (any unit in the set 2+ levels lower than the tactic's age).
metadata.cardTextSource: Exact 2015 card texts reconstructed from the official digital-edition localization strings (MilitaryCards_card_texts / MilitaryCards_card_names, Russian localization repo yashcherU/Through-the-Ages_ru, which mirrors the shipped English strings 1:1), cross-checked against namu_military.txt, faq_v15.pdf and throughtheages.fandom.com. The digital edition implements the 2015 base rules exactly; expansion-only keys were excluded.
metadata.aggressionRules: Played as a political action against one opponent. Attacker pays the card's military action cost and reveals the card. The defender may add defense: military bonus cards (defense value in the upper half) plus any number of military cards discarded face down for +1 each; the total number of bonus cards played + cards discarded may not exceed the defender's military action total (2015 change: no unit sacrifice). Attacker strength > defender strength + defense bonus => the card's effect applies; otherwise the aggression fails and the card is discarded with no effect.
metadata.warRules: Declared as a political action; resolved at the start of the declarer's next turn, before the Politics Phase. No defense bonuses and no sacrifices at resolution (2015 change). Either side can be the victor: the victor is whoever has the strictly higher strength rating at resolution; the difference is the strength advantage fed into the card's formula. Equal strength = no effect, card discarded. Spoils are capped by what the loser actually has. If the target resigns, the declarer scores 7 culture.
metadata.pactRules: Offered as a political action to a specific player, naming which side (A/B) each takes if the pact is asymmetric. The other player may accept (it takes effect immediately, placed between the two play areas) or refuse (it returns to the offerer's hand). A player may be a party to several pacts but may have only ONE pact of his or her own in play: offering a new one automatically cancels the previous one. You may also spend a political action to cancel any pact you are party to. Unless a pact says otherwise it does not prevent attacks and survives them. Pacts become obsolete (discarded) at the end of their age. REMOVED FROM THE MILITARY DECKS ENTIRELY IN 2-PLAYER GAMES.
metadata.colonizationRules: A territory card revealed as the current event is auctioned. Bids are whole numbers, each higher than the last; you may not bid more than the maximum colonization force you can send. The winner must send a force of at least the winning bid: sacrifice one or more military units (their yellow tokens return to the yellow bank) and sum their strength, add any armies' tactical strength, add colonization modifiers from cards in play, and add the colonization value of any military bonus cards played. Effects that modify the strength RATING (Alexander the Great, Great Wall, Warfare, ...) do not apply to a colonization force, and arenas cannot be sent. If nobody bids, the territory goes to the past events pile. The winner takes the card as a colony: apply the permanent effect first, then the immediate benefit. Losing a colony later (Independence Declaration, Aggression: Annex) removes the permanent effect only.
metadata.militaryBonusCardRules: A military bonus card is never 'played' for an action. Its upper half gives a defense bonus when you defend against an aggression; its lower half gives a colonization bonus when you send a colonization force. Both halves are on every card; you use whichever applies. 6 per age in the base game.
metadata.eventRules: Events are prepared, not played: as a political action you put one event or territory card from your hand face down on the FUTURE events deck and score culture equal to its age (Age A 0 / I 1 / II 2 / III 3). Doing so immediately reveals the top card of the CURRENT events deck, which is resolved and then goes to the past events pile. When the current events deck runs out, the future events deck is shuffled to become the new current events deck, with older-age cards always placed on top so they come up first. Ties in 'strongest/weakest/most' are broken in favour of the player whose turn it is (or the player closest to that player in turn order); in 2-player games 'the two strongest/weakest' is read as 'the stronger/weaker'.
metadata.ageIIIScoringEvents: In the 2015 edition ALL 15 Age III events are scoring events: each describes a way to score culture, they may be revealed during play, and every Age III event still in the current or future events decks is evaluated at the end of the game (order irrelevant; events from older ages have no effect at final scoring). There is no set of exactly four designated scoring events in the base 2015 full game -- the 2006 edition set aside 4 random Age III events at setup, and the 2015 'Shorter Game' variant deals 2 face-down + 3 face-up Age III events. Only Impact of Science and Impact of Strength are RANKING events (10/0, 14/7/0, 15/10/5/0).

civilActionCards.roster: 14 distinct yellow action cards, 33 age-variants: Age A 7 names, Age I 8, Age II 10, Age III 8. Confirmed identical in the fandom 'Card List: Digital Edition' page, the digital-edition localization string keys (RICH_LAND_0..3 etc.) and faq_v15.pdf p.12 (which groups all 14 by type).

perAgeTotals.source: civil deck sizes: Age A 20 cards, Ages I/II/III 53 cards each at 4 players (44 + 6 cards marked '3+' + 3 cards marked '4'), total 179 civil cards (czechgames.com component list). Subtracting 6 leaders + 4 wonders per age and the civil technologies (30 per age at 4 players) leaves 10/13/13/13 action cards.

civilActionCards.playerCountTrimming: Action cards carry no '3+'/'4' corner marks: all 9 cards removed from each of Civil I/II/III for 2 players (3 of them for 3 players) are technologies, so every action card's count is the same for 2, 3 and 4 players.
civilActionCards.ageACivilDeck: The Age A civil deck is exactly 20 cards = 6 Age A leaders + 4 Age A wonders + 10 action cards. The six Age A technologies (Warriors, Agriculture, Bronze, Philosophy, Religion, Despotism) are printed on the player boards and are NOT in the deck, which is why data/cards_civil.json gives them count 0. 13 of these 20 cards are dealt to the card row at setup; the rest feed the first replenish, after which the remainder goes back in the box (RB p.4/p.8).
civilActionCards.playerCountScaledEffects: Wave of Nationalism (II) and Military Build-Up (III) give resources for military units per stronger civilization, and Endowment for the Arts (III) gives culture per civilization with more culture: the printed amount depends on the player count (2p/3p/4p = 6/3/2 for Wave of Nationalism and Endowment, 8/5/3 for Military Build-Up).

metadata.scoringEvents: All 15 Age III events are scoring events (the 'Impact of ...' cards). They are evaluated after the last turn from both the current and the future events decks (CoL p.1, RB p.23); Age I/II events left in those decks are ignored. Every Age III event in this file carries "scoringEvent": true.
